text.p: Ford Motor Co told analysts Wednesday it is "on track" to meet its goal of cutting total automotive costs in 1997 by $1 billion.

In the first quarter, Ford said its automotive costs fell by $800 million from a year ago, giving it a "fast start" on its cost reduction initiatives. However, the company cautioned the improvements stem from early implemenation of cost-reduction measures and do not necessarily reflect incremental savings. Lower costs and high margins enabled Ford to post first quarter earnings of $1.20 a fully diluted share, up from $0.53 a year ago.

In the first period, Ford's auto operations had a 5.1 percent return on sales in North America, an improvement of 4.4 percent from a year ago. It has targeted a four percent return on sales for all of 1997.
Ford also cut first quarter capital spending to $1.6 billion from $1.8 billion. The automaker wants to hold 1997 capital spending on an absolute basis to its 1996 level.
In other news, Ford said it plans to accelerate the introduction of the new Lincoln Town Car to October from November.
